ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari, partly citing Hasan, says courtiers restrained Pharaoh by portraying Moses as a weak magician and warning that killing him would make people think Pharaoh could not answer his proof.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وبعضه من كلام الحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan thinks Pharaoh knew Moses was a prophet and that his signs were not magic; he was murderous and tyrannical but feared immediate destruction if he killed Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن فرعون، لعنه الله، كان قد استيقن أنه نبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r5.claim: Let him call his Lord betrays Pharaoh's fear of Moses and his prayer; the call to let me kill him was a show for his subjects, while inner terror alone held him back.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r5.anchor: شاهد صدق على فرط خوفه منه ومن دعوته ربه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya says Moses' signs shook Pharaoh's standing and his followers' beliefs; the plea to let him act is not the speech of a ruler assured of obedience, and the believer's open challenge reflects belief in Moses' prophethood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p249/r6.anchor: فليست هذه من ألفاظ الجبابرة المتمكنين من إنفاذ أوامرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r1.claim: Pharaoh feigns concern for his subjects by claiming that Moses might change their religion or cause corruption; here din means sovereignty, supported by Zuhayr's use of the word.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r1.anchor: في دين عمرو وحالت بيننا فدك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r2.claim: Changing their religion means overturning Pharaoh's worship and their idolatry; corruption means disorder, insecurity, ruined livelihoods, and deaths, so Pharaoh claims to fear harm to religion and worldly life.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r3.claim: Pharaoh mentions religion before worldly change because his subjects' attachment to their religion exceeds their attachment to wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r3.anchor: وبدأ فرعون بخوفه تغيير دينهم على تغيير دنياهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r4.claim: The phrase ذروني implies others were stopping Pharaoh, perhaps because one believed Moses, because of Hasan's explanation, or to keep the ruler occupied and protect themselves from his harm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r4.anchor: وقيل: ذروني يدل على أنهم كانوا يمنعونه من قتله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r5.claim: Kufan readers use أو أن to make Pharaoh fear either religious change or corruption; the rest of the seven use وإن and make the fear apply to both.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r5.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون: أو أن، بترديد الخوف بين تبديل الدين أو ظهور الفساد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r6.claim: Several readers vocalize يظهر from أظهر with الفساد in the accusative; other readers use ظهر with الفساد nominative, Mujahid doubles the consonants, and Zayd ibn Ali reads the passive with nominative الفساد.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p250/r6.anchor: وقرأ أنس بن مالك، وابن المسيب، ومجاهد، وقتادة، وأبو رجاء

STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.claim: Verses 10–20 warn of the disbelievers’ Hereafter; this sets up the extended Moses and Pharaoh account, centered on a believer in Pharaoh’s House challenging opposition to Moses.
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.anchor: Vv. 10–20 then tell of the place of the disbelievers in the Hereafter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r5.claim: The Moses–Pharaoh account warns Quraysh, encourages Muhammad and his companions to endure trials until victory, and profiles a Pharaoh’s family believer as a lesson for Quraysh and hesitant sympathizers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r5.anchor: A specific part of the account of Moses (sws) and the Pharaoh is recounted so that a reminder can be sounded

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p26/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p26/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p26/r2.claim: The Moses and Pharaoh story supports the prior claim that a people rejecting their messenger are destroyed despite worldly grandeur, and assures the Prophet and companions to persevere in their duty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p26/r2.anchor: when a messenger is sent to a nation and it denies him, then it is necessarily destroyed however much it may be superior

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p31/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p31/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p31/r1.claim: After the scheme failed and Moses’ demand unsettled them, Pharaoh asked his courtiers to let him kill Moses and taunted Moses to call on his Lord for help.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p31/r1.anchor: the Pharaoh sought permission from his courtiers to slay Moses (sws) and if he has a Lord who has sent him forth as His messenger, then he should call Him for help

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p31/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p31/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p31/r2.claim: Pharaoh claimed to fear Moses would change their religion or cause rebellion: monotheism challenged Pharaoh’s divine kingship, while Israelite organization could threaten the state.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p31/r2.anchor: the Pharaoh was regarded by his people to be the manifestation of the sun God and his state was that of an incarnate king

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p31/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p31/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p31/r3.claim: The wording let me shows Moses and his call had become so powerful that even a tyrant like Pharaoh could not seize him without his chiefs’ help.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p31/r3.anchor: Moses (sws) and his call had acquired such might that it was not possible for even a tyrant and dictator like Pharaoh to seize him without the help of his chiefs

IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r8.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r8.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r8.claim: Mujahid lists added yāʾs left unvowelled before a separate alif when attached to a jussive verb, including فاذكروني أذكركم and رب فأنظرني.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r8.anchor: ومما ترك تحريك يائه عند الألف المقطوعة المتصلة بالفعل المجزوم قوله ﴿ فاذكروني أذكركم ﴾ البقرة 152

RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r1.claim: On the second possibility, no one actually prevented Pharaoh from killing Moses; Pharaoh feared that a miracle would stop him and expose his fear, so he blustered to conceal it from his followers.
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r1.anchor: والاحتمال الثاني : أن أحدا ما منع فرعون من قتل موسى

RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r2.claim: Pharaoh's words “let him call his Lord” are mockery: he says he will kill Moses and dares him to call on his Lord for rescue.
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r2.anchor: أما قوله { وليدع ربه } فإنما ذكره على سبيل الاستهزاء

RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads the yāʾ in “let me” with fatḥa.
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r3.anchor: فتح ابن كثير الياء من قوله { ذرونى }

RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r4.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, and Abū ʿAmr read the yāʾ in “I fear” with fatḥa.
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r4.anchor: وفتح نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو الياء من { إنى أخاف }

RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r5.speaker: نافع وابن عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r5.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿAmr read with wāw and omit “or,” coordinating both outcomes: altering the religion and manifesting corruption.
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r5.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عمرو { وإن يظهروا } بالواو وبحذف أو

RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r6.speaker: الذين قرأوا بصيغة أو
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r6.claim: Readers who retain “or” mean that one of the two outcomes must occur.
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r6.anchor: والذين قرأوا بصيغة أو فمعناه أنه لا بد من وقع أحد الأمرين

RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r7.speaker: قُرِئ
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r7.claim: A reading with ḍamma on yāʾ, kasra on hāʾ, and accusative “corruption” makes the verb transitive: Moses would cause corruption to appear.
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r7.anchor: وقرىء يظهر بضم الياء وكسر الهاء والفساد بالنصب على التعدية

RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r8.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r8.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read “or corruption appears” with fatḥa and nominative “corruption”; if Moses changes religion, its resulting corruption appears.
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r8.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم بلفظ أو يظهر بفتح الياء والهاء والفساد بالرفع

RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r9.claim: Pharaoh alleges that Moses' success would corrupt religion or worldly order: Egyptians regarded their own religion as true, and Moses could gather followers, spark disputes, and stir up strife; religion comes first because people prize it above wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v27p48/r9.anchor: المقصود من هذا الكلام بيان السبب الموجب لقتله

STUDYQURAN:40:23/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r19.speaker: IJ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r19.claim: Pharaoh’s “Leave me” implies that some retinue members feared Moses and warned against killing him, sensing he would destroy them.
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r19.anchor: among Pharaoh’s retinue were some who feared Moses and warned against killing him, sensing that Moses would bring destruction upon them (IJ, Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:40:23/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r20.speaker: IJ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r20.claim: Pharaoh’s professed fear of changed religion means fear Moses would turn people from worshipping Pharaoh and believing in his divinity.
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r20.anchor: turn them away from their worship of Pharaoh himself (IJ) and their belief in his divinity(Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:40:23/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r21.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r21.claim: The corruption charge echoes Pharaoh’s notables in 7:127.
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r21.anchor: The accusation that Moses will cause corruption to appear in the land reflects the question posed to Pharaoh by his notables in 7:127

STUDYQURAN:40:23/r23.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r23.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r23.claim: Those spreading corruption present themselves as righteous and opponents as corrupt, as in 2:11; 30:41 is cited for the broader theme.
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r23.anchor: those who work corruption cast themselves as the righteous and their opponents as the corrupt, as in 2:11

TAB-FULL:v20p308/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r1.claim: Pharaoh tells his court to let him kill Moses and let Moses call the Lord he claims sent him to protect him; Pharaoh says Moses will change their religion by his magic.
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r1.anchor: يغير دينكم الذي أنتم عليه بسحره

TAB-FULL:v20p308/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r2.speaker: قراء المدينة والشام والبصرة
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r2.claim: Most readers in Medina, Syria, and Basra read وأن without an alif, as in the Medinan codices.
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r2.anchor: قرأ ذلك عامة قراء المدينة والشام والبصرة: (وأن يظهر في الأرض الفساد)

TAB-FULL:v20p308/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r3.speaker: قراء الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r3.claim: Most Kufan readers read أو أن with an alif, as in their codices, and read يظهر with a fatḥa on yāʾ and الفساد in the nominative.
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r3.anchor: وقرأ ذلك عامة قراء الكوفة: {أو أن} [هود: 87] بالألف،

TAB-FULL:v20p308/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r4.claim: Al-Tabari accepts both widespread conjunction readings as close in meaning: whether corruption is made manifest or appears, an agent's manifestation is implicit.
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r4.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندنا أنهما قراءتان مشهورتان

TAB-FULL:v20p308/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r5.claim: Pharaoh feared Moses would change their religion or openly establish worship of his Lord in Egypt, which Pharaoh considered corruption; replacing their religion with its opposite amounted to making corruption appear.
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r5.anchor: ففي القراءة بإحدى القراءتين في ذلك دليل واضح على صحة معنى الأخرى،

TAB-FULL:v20p308/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r6.claim: Qatada glosses their religion as the affair or condition they currently follow.
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، {إني أخاف أن يبدل دينكم} [غافر: 26]

TAB-FULL:v20p308/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r7.claim: Qatada says that for Pharaoh, corruption meant acting in obedience to God.
TAB-FULL:v20p308/r7.anchor: عن قتادة، {إني أخاف أن يبدل دينكم} [غافر: 26] «أي أمركم الذي أنتم عليه» {أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد}

BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r1.claim: ذَروني means ‘leave me alone’; Bursevī cites the lexicon’s note that the verb’s past, verbal noun, and active participle are not used.
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r1.anchor: خلوا عني واتركوني يقال : ذره ؛ أي : دعه

BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r2.claim: Pharaoh claims that killing Moses is necessary for his rule; his courtiers repeatedly restrain him, calling Moses weak and only a magician.
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r2.anchor: فإني أعلم أن صلاح ملكي في قتله

BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r3.claim: The courtiers warn that killing Moses would make people suspect Pharaoh had failed to answer his proof and resorted to the sword.
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r3.anchor: إذا قتلته أدخلت على الناس شبهة

BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r4.claim: Pharaoh pretends his courtiers alone keep him from killing Moses, but what actually restrains him is his overwhelming private fear.
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r4.anchor: وما كان الذي يكفه إلا ما في نفسه من الفزع الهائل

BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r5.claim: Pharaoh was convinced Moses was a prophet, yet feared that killing him would bring immediate destruction.
BURSEVI:v8p131#3/r5.anchor: ولكن كان يخاف إن هم بقتله أن يعاجل بالهلاك

BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r1.claim: Pharaoh taunts Moses to call on the Lord he claims sent him to protect him; Pharaoh outwardly fears Moses and inwardly fears his prayer.
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r1.anchor: وهو يخاف منه ظاهرا ويخاف من دعاء ربه باطنا

BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r2.claim: Changing their religion means replacing their worship of Pharaoh and idols, which they worship as a means of drawing near to God.
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r2.anchor: بغير ما أنتم عليه من الدين الذي هو عبارة عن عبادته وعبادة الأصنام لتقربهم إليه

BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r3.claim: If Moses cannot change their religion entirely, Pharaoh alleges he may bring worldly disorder through conflict and violence; ‘or’ offers either alternative.
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r3.anchor: ما يفسد دنياكم من التحارب والتهارج إن لم يقدر

BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r4.claim: Blind-hearted Pharaoh imagines God or his people will let him kill Moses, not realizing God will destroy him and his people and save Moses and his people.
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r4.anchor: ظن أن الله يذره أن يقتل موسى بحوله وقوته أو يذره قومه

BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r5.claim: Pharaoh fears a change of religion and earthly disorder, but not the destruction of himself and his people or the ruin of their condition in both worlds.
BURSEVI:v8p131#4/r5.anchor: ولم يخاف هلاك نفسه وهلاك قومه وفساد حالهم في الدارين

TABATABAI:40:21-26/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:21-26/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:21-26/r15.claim: Dharūnī means “leave me alone”; Pharaoh addresses his council.
TABATABAI:40:21-26/r15.anchor: أي اتركوني، خطاب يخاطب به ملأه

TABATABAI:40:21-26/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:21-26/r16.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:21-26/r16.claim: Pharaoh’s words suggest that people around him were advising him not to kill Moses and to desist from harming him.
TABATABAI:40:21-26/r16.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أنه كان هناك قوم يشيرون عليه أن لا يقتل موسى

TABATABAI:40:26-28/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r2.claim: Pharaoh taunts Moses arrogantly: let him call on his Lord to rescue him from my hand and death, if he can.
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r2.anchor: كلمة قالها كبرا وعتوا يقول اتركوني أقتله وليدع ربه فلينجه من يدي

TABATABAI:40:26-28/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r3.claim: Pharaoh alleges that Moses would replace idol worship with worship of God alone.
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r3.anchor: أما من جهة دينهم - وهو عبادة الأصنام - فأن يبدله ويضع موضعه عبادة الله وحده

TABATABAI:40:26-28/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r4.claim: The worldly danger Pharaoh alleges is Moses gaining followers and strength, provoking revolt, conflict, war, and insecurity.
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r4.anchor: فكأن يعظم أمره ويتقوى جانبه ويكثر متبعوه فيتظاهروا بالتمرد والمخالفة فيؤول الأمر إلى المشاجرة والقتال وانسلاب الأمن

TABATABAI:40:21-54/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:21-54/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:40:21-54/r1.claim: In al-ʿIlal, Imam al-Ṣādiq says Pharaoh’s prudence restrained him; prophets and their descendants are not killed except those born of fornication.
TABATABAI:40:21-54/r1.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قول فرعون { ذروني أقتل موسى } ما كان يمنعه

TABRISI:40:26-28/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:26-28/r1.speaker: أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو
TABRISI:40:26-28/r1.claim: The readers of Medina and Abū ʿAmr read وأن يظهر with a causative verb and الفساد in the accusative.
TABRISI:40:26-28/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو وأن يظهر بغير ألف قبل الواو ويظهر بضم الياء وكسر الهاء الفساد بالنصب

TABRISI:40:26-28/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:26-28/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر
TABRISI:40:26-28/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read وإن يظهر with يظهر opened and الفساد nominative.
TABRISI:40:26-28/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر وإن يظهر بفتح الياء الفساد بالرفع

TABRISI:40:26-28/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:26-28/r3.speaker: حفص ويعقوب
TABRISI:40:26-28/r3.claim: Ḥafṣ and Yaʿqūb read أو أن يظهر with ḍamma on yāʾ and accusative الفساد.
TABRISI:40:26-28/r3.anchor: وقرأ حفص ويعقوب أو أن يظهر بضم الياء الفساد بالنصب

TABRISI:40:26-28/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:26-28/r4.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:40:26-28/r4.claim: The remaining readers read أو أن يظهر with fatḥa on yāʾ and nominative الفساد.
TABRISI:40:26-28/r4.anchor: والباقون أو أن يظهر بفتح الياء الفساد بالرفع

TABRISI:40:26-28/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:26-28/r5.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:40:26-28/r5.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains أو أن as one kind of feared action, like saying eat bread or dates, whereas وإن makes two separate things feared.
TABRISI:40:26-28/r5.anchor: قال أبو علي: من قرأ أو أن يظهر فالمعنى إني أخاف هذا الضرب منه

TABRISI:40:26-28/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:26-28/r6.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:40:26-28/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the causative reading makes Moses the agent, parallel to the preceding threat to change their religion; the intransitive reading makes corruption appear in the land.
TABRISI:40:26-28/r6.anchor: ومن قرأ يظهر في الأرض الفساد فأسند الفعل إلى موسى

TABRISI:40:26-28/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:26-28/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:26-28/r9.claim: Pharaoh tells his people to leave him to kill Moses, implying that some of his intimates had urged him not to do so and feared Moses might pray and destroy him.
TABRISI:40:26-28/r9.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه كان في خاصة فرعون قوم يشيرون عليه بأن لا يقتل موسى

TABRISI:40:26-28/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:26-28/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:26-28/r10.claim: Pharaoh means they should tell Moses to call on his Lord for help in escaping death, since Pharaoh arrogantly claims the prayer will do nothing.
TABRISI:40:26-28/r10.anchor: معناه وقولوا له ليدع ربه وليستعن به في دفع القتل عنه

TABRISI:40:26-28/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:26-28/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:40:26-28/r11.claim: An alternative says Pharaoh's people called Moses a sorcerer and feared killing him before proof appeared would strengthen suspicion, so they proposed delaying and summoning the magicians.
TABRISI:40:26-28/r11.anchor: وقيل: إنهم قالوا له هو ساحر فإن قتلته قبل ظهور الحجة

TABRISI:40:26-28/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:26-28/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:26-28/r12.claim: Pharaoh fears Moses will change the religion of his people, meaning their belief in Pharaoh's gods.
TABRISI:40:26-28/r12.anchor: إن لم أقتله وهو ما تعتقدونه من إلهتي

TABRISI:40:26-28/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:26-28/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:26-28/r13.claim: Pharaoh claims Moses may gain followers and provoke fighting that devastates the land and brings disorder.
TABRISI:40:26-28/r13.anchor: بأن يتبعه قوم ويحتاج إلى أن نقاتله فيخرب فيما بين ذلك البلاد ويظهر الفساد

TABRISI:40:26-28/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:26-28/r14.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:40:26-28/r14.claim: Qatāda says Pharaoh considered obedience to God to be corruption.
TABRISI:40:26-28/r14.anchor: وقيل: إن الفساد عند فرعون أن يعمل بطاعة الله عن قتادة

THALABI:v8p272/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p272/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p272/r2.claim: Pharaoh says Moses may call on the Lord he claims sent him, challenging that Lord to protect him from Pharaoh.
THALABI:v8p272/r2.anchor: وليَدْعُ ربه الذي يزعم أنه أرسله إلينا فيمنعه منا

THALABI:v8p272/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p272/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو وأهل المدينة وأهل الشام وأهل مكة
THALABI:v8p272/r3.claim: Abu Amr and the readers of Medina, Syria, and Mecca read wa-an without an alif after the conjunction; their regional codices likewise lack it.
THALABI:v8p272/r3.anchor: قرأ أبو عمر وأهل المدينة وأهل الشام وأهل مكة: وأن بغير ألف، وكذلك هي في مصاحف أهل الحرمين والشام.

THALABI:v8p272/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p272/r4.speaker: الكوفيون وبعض البصريين
THALABI:v8p272/r4.claim: The Kufans and some Basrans read aw-an with the alif, matching the Iraqi codices.
THALABI:v8p272/r4.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون وبعض البصريين: (أو أن) بالألف، وكذلك هي في مصاحف أهل العراق.

THALABI:v8p272/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p272/r5.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v8p272/r5.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers aw-an: its extra letter supports that reading, and aw can sometimes carry the sense of waw, whereas waw cannot mean aw.
THALABI:v8p272/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: وبها يقرأ للزيادة التي فيها،

THALABI:v8p272/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p272/r6.speaker: أهل المدينة والبصرة وحفص عن عاصم
THALABI:v8p272/r6.claim: Medina and Basra, and Hafs from Asim, read the verb causatively and put corruption in the accusative.
THALABI:v8p272/r6.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والبصرة: (يظهر) بضم الياء وكسر الهاء، و (الفساد) بنصب الدال على التعدية.

THALABI:v8p272/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p272/r7.speaker: الآخرون
THALABI:v8p272/r7.claim: The other readers use an intransitive form and put corruption in the nominative; Abu Hatim selects this reading.
THALABI:v8p272/r7.anchor: على اللزوم، وهي اختيار أبي حاتم.

THALABI:v8p272/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p272/r8.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
THALABI:v8p272/r8.claim: Abu Ubayd favors the transitive reading because it parallels change your religion; Abu Hatim favors the intransitive reading.
THALABI:v8p272/r8.anchor: وهي اختيار أبي عبيد قال لقومه: يبدل دينكم، فكذلك يظهر ليكون الفعلان على نسق واحد.

THALABI:v8p272/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p272/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p272/r9.claim: Fasad means the decline of affairs; Pharaoh meant changing their religion and worshipping another.
THALABI:v8p272/r9.anchor: والفساد انتقاص الأمر، وأراد فرعون به تبديل الدين وعبادة غيره

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:25-29/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:25-29/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:25-29/r3.claim: Pharaoh tells his chiefs to let him kill Moses and challenges Moses to call on the Lord who sent him to protect him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:25-29/r3.anchor: وقال فرعون } لملئه: { ذروني أقتل موسى وليدع ربه } الذي أرسله إلينا، فيمنعه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:25-29/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:25-29/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:25-29/r4.claim: Pharaoh claims to fear that Moses will abolish their religion or corrupt it for them if he cannot abolish it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:25-29/r4.anchor: الذين أنتم عليه يبطله { أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد } أو يفسد عليكم دينكم إن لم يبطله

ELMALILI:40:21-27/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:21-27/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:21-27/r1.claim: Pharaoh’s threat is an example of the earlier statement that every community plotted against its messenger.

ELMALILI:40:21-27/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:21-27/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:21-27/r2.claim: Moses’ miracles had broken Pharaoh’s despotism: he was confused and could no longer do as he wished.
ELMALILI:40:21-27/r2.anchor: Hazret-i Mûsâ’nın mu‘cizâtı karşısında Firavun’un istibdâdı kırılmış, dilediğini yapamaz olmuş ve şaşırmıştı

ELMALILI:40:21-27/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:21-27/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:21-27/r3.claim: The account in al-Aʿrāf suggests the matter had moved beyond consulting the public to an intervention, prompting Pharaoh to shout that they should let him act.
ELMALILI:40:21-27/r3.anchor: mesele cemiyetin yalnız re’yine müracaattan ibaret kalmamış, bir müdahale mâhiyetini almış olmalı ki “bırakın beni” diye bağırıyor

ELMALILI:40:21-27/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:21-27/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:21-27/r4.claim: Pharaoh tries to deny or mock God by saying Moses should call on his Lord, yet presents himself as pious by warning that Moses will change their religion.
ELMALILI:40:21-27/r4.anchor: bir taraftan da “dininizi değiştirecek” diye dindarlık gösteriyor

ELMALILI:40:21-27/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:21-27/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:21-27/r5.claim: Elmalılı speculates that the God Pharaoh calls his own may be his sovereignty.
ELMALILI:40:21-27/r5.anchor: Belki onun Allah dediği kendi saltanatıdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:25/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:25/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:25/r2.claim: Ancient Egyptian tradition treated Pharaoh as king and son of a god, hence a god; he likely feared Moses’ beliefs would threaten that religion and his position, and decided to kill Moses and massacre the male children of his followers (as Ibn Atiyya interprets the verses).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:25/r2.anchor: Firavunlar hem kral hem de tanrının oğlu, dolayısıyla tanrı sayılıyorlardı. İşte Firavun, muhtemelen, Mûsâ’nın sözünü ettiği dinî inançların kendi halkının geleneksel dinî telakkisini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:25/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:25/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:25/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya also reads Pharaoh’s stated fear as a concern that Moses would change the people’s religion or cause unrest in the land.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:25/r3.anchor: Nitekim İbn Atıyye de söz konusu âyetleri bu yönde yorumlamaktadır (IV, 555).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:25/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:25/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:25/r4.claim: Despite the danger, Moses trusted that God would help those who believe and persevere on the right path, against despots who think their deeds go unpunished because they deny the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:25/r4.anchor: Hz. Mûsâ, âhirete inanmadıkları için yaptıklarının yanlarına kalacağını sanan bütün despotik güçlere karşı Allah’ın, kendisine inanıp güvenerek doğru yolda azimle ilerleyenlere yardım edeceğinden emindi.

BAQILLANI:v1p167/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r1.claim: Bāqillānī judges the sexual boast in Imruʾ al-Qays's first quoted line obscene, pointless, repellent to listeners, and lacking either fine expression or good meaning.
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r1.anchor: فالبيت الأول غاية في الفحش ونهاية في السخف وأي فائدة لذكره لعشيقته

BAQILLANI:v1p167/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r2.claim: The next line about a beloved's refusal is badly woven and offers no useful reason to report that she resisted him at a named place.
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r2.anchor: فهو كلام رديء النسج لا فائدة لذكره لنا أن حبيبته تمنعت عليه يوما بموضع يسميه

BAQILLANI:v1p167/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r3.claim: He finds the line addressed to Fāṭima limp and effeminate; the defense that feminine verse suits women's nature fails because poets retain firmness in feminine poetry.
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r3.anchor: فالبيت الأول فيه ركاكة جدا وتأنيث ورقة ولكن فيها تخنيث

BAQILLANI:v1p167/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r4.claim: The second hemistich does not fit the first or its preceding verse, and scolding a beloved for coyness conflicts with the lover's delight in it.
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r4.anchor: والمصراع الثاني منقطع عن الأول لا يلائمه ولا يوافقه

BAQILLANI:v1p167/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r5.claim: The line claiming that the beloved's commands govern the speaker's heart is criticized as inconsistent with his earlier displays of love and weeping, unless it shifts to an incompatible pose of toughness.
BAQILLANI:v1p167/r5.anchor: فهذا خلاف ما أظهر من نفسه فيما تقدم من الأبيات من الحب والبكاء على الأحبة

BURHAN:v1p140/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p140/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p140/r6.claim: أو أن, with hamza before waw, occurs in Hud, Bani Israil, Ta Ha, and al-Mumin; examples include Hud and al-Mumin.

ITQAN:v4p315/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p315/r1.speaker: آخرون
ITQAN:v4p315/r1.claim: Some say the Qur’an’s ancient narratives are miraculous because they recount events as an eyewitness would.
ITQAN:v4p315/r1.anchor: وقال آخرون ما تضمنه من الإخبار عن قصص الأولين وسائر المتقدمين حكاية من شاهدها وحضرها

ITQAN:v4p315/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p315/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
ITQAN:v4p315/r3.claim: Qadi Abu Bakr says inimitability lies in arrangement beyond Arab patterns; poetic devices are learnable, but this structure has no model and cannot arise by chance.
ITQAN:v4p315/r3.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر وجه إعجازه ما فيه من النظم والتأليف والترصيف وأنه خارج عن جميع وجوه النظم المعتاد في كلام العرب

ITQAN:v4p315/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p315/r4.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
ITQAN:v4p315/r4.claim: Qadi Abu Bakr adds that the miracle is more obvious in some passages and subtler in others.
ITQAN:v4p315/r4.anchor: ونحن نعتقد أن الإعجاز في بعض القرآن أظهر وفي بعضه أدق وأغمض

ITQAN:v4p315/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p315/r5.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
ITQAN:v4p315/r5.claim: Al-Razi identifies the miracle as eloquence, unusual style, and freedom from defects.
ITQAN:v4p315/r5.anchor: وقال الإمام فخر الدين وجه الإعجاز الفصاحة وغرابة الأسلواب والسلامة من جميع العيوب

ITQAN:v4p315/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p315/r6.speaker: الزملكاني
ITQAN:v4p315/r6.claim: Al-Zamalkani locates the miracle in unique composition, with words balanced in grammar and measure and meanings at the highest level.
ITQAN:v4p315/r6.anchor: وقال الزملكاني وجه الإعجاز راجع إلى التأليف الخاص به لا مطلق التأليف بأن اعتدلت مفرداته تركيبا وزنة

ITQAN:v4p315/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p315/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ITQAN:v4p315/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya says inimitability comes from arrangement, sound meanings, and eloquent wording: God selects every word with full knowledge, while human ignorance and forgetfulness prevent matching it.
ITQAN:v4p315/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عطية الصحيح والذي عليه الجمهور والحذاق في وجه إعجازه أنه بنظمه وصحة معانيه وتوالي فصاحة ألفاظه

ITQAN:v4p315/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p315/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ITQAN:v4p315/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects that Arabs could make a counterpart but were diverted; unlike a human poem revised repeatedly, no Qur’anic word can be improved.
ITQAN:v4p315/r8.anchor: وبهذا يبطل قول من قال إن العرب كان في قدرتها الإتيان بمثله فصرفوا عن ذلك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r1.claim: Reverse comparison works when the likeness is an ordinary shared feature; it fails when the poet’s aim is to exaggerate by making the lesser thing seem superior.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r1.anchor: متى لم يقصد ضرب من المبالغة في إثبات الصفة للشىء والقصد إلى إيهام في الناقص انه كالزائد

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r2.speaker: محمد بن وهيب
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r2.claim: Muhammad b. Wahb reverses the comparison so the caliph’s face is the original and dawn the derivative, implying the face surpasses dawn in light.

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r3.claim: This conceit praises indirectly: the speaker treats dawn as so honored that it would be an achievement for dawn to resemble the caliph’s face, avoiding overt self-conscious boasting.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r3.anchor: وهو انه كان يستكثر للصباح أن يشبهه بوجه الخليفة ويوهم انه قد احتشد له واجتهد في طلب تشبيه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r4.claim: Jurjani says the indirect praise gives a special delight, like a gift unspoiled by reminders of the giver’s favor.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p194/r4.anchor: فكانت كالنعمة لم تكدرها المنة والصنيعة لم ينغصها اعتداد المصطنع لها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r1.claim: The moon verse’s wording is imprecise: absence means a gap between appearances, but the waning moon still appears each night until conjunction.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r1.anchor: فإن الأغباب أن يتخلل وقتي الحضور وقت يخلو منه وإنما يصلح لأن يراد أن القمر إذا نقص نوره

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r2.speaker: ابن بابك
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r2.claim: Ibn Babak offers a similar moon conceit, depicting it as veiling itself when it fears the coming dark moon.

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r3.claim: Poets draw comparisons from the moon’s relation to the sun and its waxing, waning, fullness, and disappearance; Ibn Nubatah’s verse uses this pattern as a subtle conceit about past rulers and a praised patron.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r3.anchor: وهكذا ينظر إلى مقابلته الشمس واستمداده من نورها وإلى كون ذلك سبب زيادته ونقصه وامتلائه من النور

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r4.speaker: ابن نباتة
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r4.claim: Ibn Nubatah compares past kings’ fading renown and the patron’s praise to the moon’s fullness after the sun and its eclipse when close to it.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r4.anchor: فمن لطيف ذلك قول ابن نباتة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r5.claim: Jurjani cites a moon comparison for the image of a patron whose light reaches the viewer wherever he turns.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r5.anchor: ومن ظهوره بكل مكان ورؤيته في كل موضع

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r6.claim: The discussion excludes visual resemblances such as a crescent’s curve or a face’s radiance, because it concerns conceptual representation.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p116/r6.anchor: فإنا في ذكر ما كان تمثيلا وكان الشبه فيه معنويا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p368/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p368/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p368/r1.claim: The same broad subject can take different semantic images: the Kharijite’s protest differs from Abū Tammām’s satire, just as al-Buḥturī’s and al-Mutanabbī’s statements about homeland differ.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p368/r1.anchor: كيف والخارجي يقول : واحتجت له فعلاته . ويقول أبو تمام :

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p368/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p368/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p368/r2.claim: Calling meanings images is a familiar scholarly analogy: distinctions in meaning resemble differences among people or crafted objects; al-Jāḥiẓ calls poetry a craft and a kind of depiction.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p368/r2.anchor: بل هو مستعمل مشهور في كلام العلماء . ويكفيك قول الجاحظ : ' وإنما الشعر صناعة وضرب من التصوير '

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p368/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p368/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p368/r3.claim: If a later poet merely repeated an unchanged meaning, judgments of improvement, failure, similarity, and hidden borrowing would be incoherent; concealment comes from recasting the meaning in a different image.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p368/r3.anchor: لو كان المعنى في أحد البيتين يكون على هيئته وصفته في البيت الآخر ، وكان التالي من الشاعرين يجيئك به معادا على وجهه

DAMGHANI:v1p173/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r3.claim: Duʿāʾ can mean seeking help or refuge, as Pharaoh says Moses may call on his Lord.
DAMGHANI:v1p173/r3.anchor: الرابع : الدعاء بمعنى الاستغاثة قوله تعالى في سورة يونس

DAMGHANI:v1p311/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p311/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p311/r4.claim: Ẓahara means to appear or become manifest: visible adornment, corruption, and what is apparent of worldly livelihood and trade.
DAMGHANI:v1p311/r4.anchor: ظهر اي بدا قوله تعالى في سورة النور ولا يبدين زينتهن الا ما ظهر منها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r1.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r1.claim: The fifth referent of al-arḍ is Egypt; examples include Pharaoh’s rule, Joseph’s office, and where corruption appears.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r1.anchor: والخامس : أرض مصر . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r2.claim: Al-arḍ can mean the land of the West; some identify the land of Gog and Magog as China.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r2.anchor: والسادس : أرض الغرب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف : ^ ( إن يأجوج ومأجوج مفسدون في الأرض ) ^ ، وقيل : أراد أرض الصين .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r3.claim: Another referent is the seven earths, as in the statement that every creature has its provision from God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r3.anchor: والسابع : الأرضون السبع . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود : ^ ( وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r4.claim: Al-arḍ can denote the land of Islam, as in the punishment of banishment.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r4.anchor: والثامن : أرض الإسلام [ ومنه قوله تعالى في المائدة ] . ^ ( ( الذين يحاربون الله ورسوله ) ويسعون في الأرض فسادا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r5.claim: A further sense is the grave, where disbelievers wish to be leveled with the earth.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r5.anchor: والتاسع : القبر . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في سورة النساء ] : ^ ( يؤمئذ يود الذين كفروا وعصوا الرسول لو تسوى بهم الأرض ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r6.claim: Al-arḍ can mean the earth at the Resurrection, illuminated by its Lord’s light.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r6.anchor: والعاشر : أرض القيامة . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في الزمر ] : ﴿ وأشرقت الأرض بنور ربها ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r7.claim: Another referent is the land of wandering, where Israelites were forbidden to enter for forty years.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r7.anchor: والحادي عشر : أرض التيه . [ ومنه ] قوله تعالى في المائدة : ﴿ قال فإنها محرمة عليهم أربعين سنة يتيهون في الأرض ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r8.claim: Al-arḍ can specifically mean Banū Qurayẓa’s territory, whose land and homes were given to the believers.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r8.anchor: والثاني عشر : أرض بني قريظة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأحزاب : ﴿ وأورثكم أرضهم وديارهم ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r9.claim: The thirteenth referent is Byzantine territory, called the nearest land in the Roman defeat passage.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p169/r9.anchor: والثالث عشر : أرض الروم . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في الروم ] : ﴿ الم غلبت الروم في أدنى الأرض ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r1.claim: Ẓuhūr is opposite hiddenness; ẓahr can mean dominance, and the verb can describe noon arriving or discovering something.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r1.anchor: الظهور : ضد الخفاء . والظهر : الغلبة . وتقول العرب : أظهرنا : إذا جاء وقت الظهر . وظهرت على الشيء : اطلعت عليه .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r2.speaker: الفرزدق
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r2.claim: Ẓuhrī describes something put behind one and thereby neglected; al-Farazdaq uses bi-ẓahr for a matter left aside.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r2.anchor: والظهري : كل شيء تجعله يظهر . أي : تنساه . ومنه قوله تعالى : ^ ( واتخذتموه وراءكم ظهريا ) ^ ، وقال الفرزدق :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r3.speaker: الفرزدق
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r3.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s phrase bi-ẓahr witnesses the sense of putting a matter behind one or neglecting it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r3.anchor: قال الفرزدق : تميم بن قيس لا تكونن حاجتي … بظهر ولا يعيا علي جوابها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r4.claim: A Qurʾanic sense is making something manifest, including corruption appearing in the land.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r4.anchor: أحدها : الإبداء . ومنه قوله تعالى في النور : ﴿ ولا يبدين زينتهن إلا ما ظهر منها ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r5.claim: A second sense is discovering or prevailing upon someone, including God’s disclosure of a secret.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r5.anchor: والثاني : الاطلاع . ومنه قوله تعالى ( في الكهف ) : ﴿ إنهم إن يظهروا عليكم يرجموكم ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r6.claim: A third sense is climbing over something, as in those unable to scale a barrier and elevated stairways.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r6.anchor: والثالث : الارتقاء . ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف : ﴿ فما اسطاعوا أن يظهروه ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r7.claim: A fourth sense is elevation and dominance, including the religion’s triumph and believers’ victory.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r7.anchor: الرابع : العلو والقهر . ومنه قوله تعلى في براءة : ﴿ ليظهره على الدين كله ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r8.claim: A fifth sense is falsehood or invalidity, exemplified by a mere apparent statement.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r8.anchor: والخامس : البطلان . ومنه قوله تعالى في الرعد : ^ ( أم بظاهر من القول ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r9.claim: Ẓuhūr can mean backs, contrasted with turning away; casting a book behind one means people did not act on it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r9.anchor: والسادس : الظهور التي يقابلها الصدود . ومنه قله تعالى في آل عمران : ﴿ فنبذوه وراء ظهورهم ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r10.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r10.claim: A seventh sense is entering the time of noon, including the afternoon prayer.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p428#2/r10.anchor: والسابع : الدخول في وقت الظهر . ومنه قوله تعالى في النور : ﴿ وحين تضعون ثيابكم من الظهيرة ﴾

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r5.claim: Āmīn is a name of God and a prayer response said after al-Fātiḥa; some exegetes derive it from a shortened “O God, answer me,” with the vocative omitted.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r5.anchor: و"آمين" اسم من أسماء الله. وقال قوم من المفسرين - في قول المصلي بعد فراغه من قراءة أم الكتاب: "آمين"-: [أمين] قصر من (3) ذلك؛ كأنه قال: يا ألله؛ وأضمر "استجب لي" -: لأنه لا يجوز أن يظهر هذا في هذا الموضع من الصلاة؛ إذ كان كلاما.- ثم تحذف ياء النداء.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r6.speaker: أصحاب اللغة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r6.claim: Language scholars prefer short-alif Amīn: they open it because it stands alone from its implicit vocative sense and has come to mean “so may God do.”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r6.anchor: وهكذا يختار أصحاب اللغة في "أمين": أن يقصروا الألف، ولا يطولوا. وأنشدوا فيه:

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r7.speaker: فطحل
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r7.claim: The poet Faṭḥal’s verse with Amīn supports the short-vowelled form preferred by the language scholars.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r7.anchor:
وأنشدوا فيه:
تباعد مني فطحل إذ سألته ... أمين, فزاد الله ما بيننا بعدا (1)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r8.speaker: قوم فصحاء
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba also records the long-alif form Āmīn from eloquent speakers.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r8.anchor: وقد أجازوا أيضا "آمين" مطولة الألف. وحكوها عن قوم فصحاء.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r9.claim: The long form is traced to yā Amīn, “O God”; the initial yāʾ was dropped for ease because the expression is frequent, like yā Zayd becoming ā Zayd, and related forms heard from eloquent Arabs.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p11/r9.anchor: وأصلها: "يا أمين" بمعنى: يا ألله. ثم تحذف همزة "أمين" استخفافا لكثرة ما تجرى هذه الكلمة على ألسنة الناس. ومخرجها مخرج "آزيد".

NAHHAS:v4p29/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p29/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p29/r16.claim: أقتل is jussive as imperative response; وليدع is an imperative, while ذروني is built though it resembles a jussive.
NAHHAS:v4p29/r16.anchor: أقتل جزم لأنه جواب الأمر ( وليدع ) جزم لأنه أمر

NAHHAS:v4p29/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p29/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p29/r17.claim: One explanation says Pharaoh had been warned that prayer against him might be answered, so he taunted Moses to call on his Lord.
NAHHAS:v4p29/r17.anchor: وقيل هذا يدل على أنه قيل لفرعون إنا نخاف أن ندعو عليك

NAHHAS:v4p29/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p29/r18.speaker: المدنيون وأبو عبد الرحمن وابن عامر وأبو عمرو
NAHHAS:v4p29/r18.claim: These readers use واو before the second أن يظهر; the Kufans use أو and Abu Ubayd argues أو may mean واو.
NAHHAS:v4p29/r18.anchor: هذه قراءة المدنيين وأبي عبد الرحمن وابن عامر وأبي عمرو

NAHHAS:v4p29/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p29/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p29/r19.claim: Al-Nahhas rejects equating أو and واو here: واو means both fears, while أو means either outcome.
NAHHAS:v4p29/r19.anchor: لأن معنى الواو إني أخاف الأمرين جميعا ومعنى أو لأحد الأمرين

SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r1.claim: The Kufans read أو أن, using أو for uncertainty; the other readers use واو coordination, making the fear govern both changing the religion and manifesting corruption.
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r1.anchor: قرأ الكوفيون " أو أن " بأو التي للإبهام والباقون بواو النسق على تسلط الحرف

SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r2.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وحفص
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r2.claim: Nafi, Abu Amr, and Hafs read يظهر with active Form IV: Moses is its subject and الفساد its accusative object.
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وحفص " يظهر " بضم الياء وكسر الهاء من أظهر، وفاعله

SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r3.speaker: باقي القراء
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r3.claim: The other readers use Form I يظهر; الفساد is nominative as its subject.
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r3.anchor: بفتح الياء والهاء من ظهر، " الفساد " رفعا بالفاعلية وزيد بن علي

SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r4.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads يظهر as a passive; الفساد is nominative as deputy subject.
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r4.anchor: وزيد بن علي " يظهر " مبنيا للمفعول، " الفساد " مرفوع لقيامه مقام الفاعل.

SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r5.speaker: مجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r5.claim: Mujahid reads يظهر with a doubled ظ and ه, derived from يتظهر by assimilation of ت into ظ; الفساد remains the subject.
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r5.anchor: ومجاهد " يظهر " بتشديد الظاء والهاء، وأصلها يتظهر من تظهر بتشديد الهاء

SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r6.speaker: ابن كثير
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the yāʾ in ذروني with fatḥ; the other readers make it quiescent.
SAMIN-DURR:40:26/r6.anchor: وفتح ابن كثير ياء { ذروني أقتل موسى } وسكنها الباقون.

ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r1.claim: Iraqi codices have aw an yuẓhira; the Hijazi codex has wa-an yuẓhira without the alif, and the latter form is also allowed.
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r1.anchor: على هذا مصاحف أهل العراق، وفي مصحف أهل الحجاز

ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r2.claim: With aw, Pharaoh presents alternatives: he fears Moses will abolish the religion, or, if not abolish it, corrupt it; Pharaoh calls obedience to God corruption.
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r2.anchor: ومعنى أو وقوع أحد الشيئيق فالمعنى على

ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r3.claim: With wa-an, Pharaoh claims to fear that the religion will be abolished and corruption will come with it.
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r3.anchor: فيكون المعنى أخاف إبطال دينكم والفساد معه

ASAD-NOTES:40:25#n18/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:40:25#n18/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:40:25#n18/r1.claim: Asad inserts "alleged" to preserve the obvious sarcasm in Pharaoh's remark about Moses invoking his Sustainer.
ASAD-NOTES:40:25#n18/r1.anchor: My interpolation of the word "alleged" is necessitated by the obvious sarcasm of Pharaoh's remark.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p900/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p900/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p900/r3.claim: Ghafir puts Pharaoh first because Moses was sent to him and the sura then focuses on him; Qarun is outside that context.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p900/r3.anchor: لمن أرسل موسى؟ لفرعون فناسب أن يكون فرعون أول المذكورين في الآية التي بعدها

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107/r1.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107/r1.claim: Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read أو أن with alif before the conjunction; another reading has وأن.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107/r1.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: أو أن [غافر/ 26] بألف قبل الواو .

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107/r2.claim: With أو, Pharaoh fears this kind of thing from Moses; أو may include both feared things, like eating bread or dates.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: من قرأ أو أن يظهر، فالمعنى: أخاف هذا الضرب منه، كما تقول: كل خبزا أو تمرا

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107/r3.claim: On the وأن reading, Pharaoh fears the two things from Moses.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107/r3.anchor: ومن قال: وأن يظهر فالمعنى: إني أخاف هذين الأمرين منه

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r1.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r1.claim: Nafi and Abu Amr read يظهر with ḍamma on yāʾ and الفساد accusative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو: ويظهر بضم الياء في الأرض الفساد نصبا.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir read يظهر with fatḥa on yāʾ and الفساد nominative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر: يظهر* منصوبة الياء في الأرض الفساد رفعا.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r3.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r3.claim: Abu Bakr's transmission from Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read أو أن يظهر with الفساد nominative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي: أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد رفعا.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r4.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r4.claim: Hafs from Asim reads أو أن يظهر with ḍamma on yāʾ and الفساد accusative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r4.anchor: حفص عن عاصم أو أن يظهر برفع الياء في الأرض الفساد نصبا .

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r5.claim: Al-Farisi says the يظهر reading best matches the preceding verb يبدل.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p107#2/r5.anchor: حجة من قال يظهر أنه أشبه بما قبله، لأن قبله: يبدل

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p313/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p313/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p313/r1.claim: Aw presents changing religion or causing corruption as one of alternatives, including doubt or allowance; wāw joins both conditions, which the author prefers as it combines them.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p313/r1.anchor: أنه جعل الحرف لأحد الحالين على طريق الشك أو الإباحة لان لأو في الكلام اربعة اوجه

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p313/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p313/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p313/r2.claim: With ḍamma on yāʾ, the verb is transitive and takes “corruption” as object, in parallel with “that he change your religion.”

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p313/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p313/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p313/r3.claim: With fatḥa on yāʾ, the intransitive verb makes “corruption” its subject: if he changes your religion, corruption will appear on earth.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p313/r3.anchor: والحجة لمن فتح الياء انه قطع الفساد وظهوره من التبديل فافرده ورفعه به ومعناه فان يبدل دينكم ظهر في الأرض الفساد

IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r1.claim: These readers read وأن يظهر without an alif before the conjunction.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر / وأن يظهر / بغير ألف قبل الواو

IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r2.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r2.claim: Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read أو أن يظهر with an alif before the conjunction; this form also appears in Kufan codices.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائى ﴿ أو أن يظهر ﴾ بألف قبل الواو وكذلك هى فى مصاحف أهل الكوفة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r3.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r3.claim: Nafi and Abu Amr read يظهر with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and الفساد in the accusative.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r3.anchor: فقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو ﴿ يظهر ﴾ مضمومة الياء ﴿ الفساد ﴾ نصبا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir read يظهر with the yāʾ described as منصوب and الفساد in the nominative.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر ﴿ يظهر ﴾ منصوبة الياء ﴿ الفساد ﴾ رفعا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r5.speaker: عاصم فى رواية أبى بكر وحمزة والكسائى
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r5.claim: Asim in Abu Bakr's transmission, Hamza, and al-Kisai read يظهر with an open yāʾ and الفساد in the nominative.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r5.anchor: قرأ عاصم فى رواية أبى بكر وحمزة والكسائى ﴿ يظهر ﴾ بفتح الياء ﴿ الفساد ﴾ رفعا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r6.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r6.claim: Hafs from Asim reads يظهر with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and الفساد in the accusative.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r6.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم ﴿ يظهر ﴾ برفع الياء ﴿ الفساد ﴾ نصبا

NASHR:v2p168/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p168/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p168/r2.claim: Readers agree to quiesce nine possessive yāʾs, including Yusuf's يدعونني إليه; some attribute this to the weight of many consecutive letters, while the source notes other explanations too.
NASHR:v2p168/r2.anchor: (واتفقوا) على: إسكان تسع ياءات من هذا الفصل، وهي في الأعراف أنظرني إلى

NASHR:v2p164/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p164/r3.speaker: ابن كثير والأصبهاني
NASHR:v2p164/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr and al-Aṣbahānī open the yāʾ in ذروني أقتل.
NASHR:v2p164/r3.anchor: واختص هو والأصبهاني بفتح ياء واحدة، وهي ذروني أقتل في غافر

NASHR:v2p365/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p365/r4.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p365/r4.claim: Among the eight yāʾs of annexation, the Madinans, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr open the yāʾ in إني أخاف at its three occurrences.
NASHR:v2p365/r4.anchor: إني أخاف في ثلاث مواضع فتحها المدنيان، وابن كثير وأبو عمرو

NASHR:v2p365/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p365/r5.speaker: ابن كثير والأصبهاني عن ورش
NASHR:v2p365/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir and al-Asbahani from Warsh open the yāʾ in ذروني أقتل.
NASHR:v2p365/r5.anchor: ذروني أقتل فتحها ابن كثير والأصبهاني عن ورش

NASHR:v1p432#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p432#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p432#2/r1.claim: At pause, a hamza after silent alif can become alif: once hamza is quiescent, the preceding alif no longer blocks substitution after fatḥa; whether the resulting alif remains before a consonant is discussed later.
NASHR:v1p432#2/r1.anchor: فإن كان ألفا، فإنه يأتي بعده كل من الحركات الثلاث

NASHR:v1p432#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p432#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p432#2/r2.claim: When hamza follows an extra silent yāʾ or wāw, it is eased by substitution with a matching letter and assimilation; examples are النسيء and بريء, and قروء.
NASHR:v1p432#2/r2.anchor: أو واوا زائدتين، فإنه لم يرد في الياء إلا في

NASHR:v1p432#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p432#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p432#2/r3.claim: After any other silent consonant, hamza is deleted and its vowel transferred to that consonant, whether it is sound, original yāʾ, or original wāw, long or lin.
NASHR:v1p432#2/r3.anchor: فتسهيله أن تنقل حركة الهمزة إلى ذلك الساكن ويحركها بها

NASHR:v1p432#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p432#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p432#2/r4.claim: The source lists seven examples after sound consonants: four with ḍamma, two with kasra, and one with fatḥa; original yāʾ and wāw examples are then grouped by long-vowel and lin status.
NASHR:v1p432#2/r4.anchor: فالساكن الصحيح ورد منه في القرآن سبعة مواضع، منها أربعة الهمزة فيها

NASHR:v1p432#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p432#2/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p432#2/r5.claim: For a moving hamza preceded by a vowel, the preceding consonant is only temporarily silent at pause; easing it, romm, and conformity to rasm are treated elsewhere.
NASHR:v1p432#2/r5.anchor: والمتطرف المتحرك المتحرك ما قبله هو الساكن العارض المتطرف

QIRAAT-ER:40:26:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:40:26:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:40:26:4#1/r1.claim: Opening the final yāʾ as -iya makes the first-person suffix fuller in recitation without changing root or syntax.
QIRAAT-ER:40:26:4#1/r1.anchor: Final yāʾ is opened as -iya, making the first-person suffix more fully vocalized

QIRAAT-ER:40:26:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:40:26:11#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:40:26:11#1/r1.claim: Opening the final yāʾ as -iya gives a fuller recitation of the first-person suffix without syntactic change.
QIRAAT-ER:40:26:11#1/r1.anchor: Final yāʾ is opened as -iya, making the first-person suffix fuller in recitation

QIRAAT-ER:40:26:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:40:26:16#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:40:26:16#1/r1.claim: The variant wa-an coordinates the two feared outcomes conjunctively instead of linking them disjunctively with aw-an.
QIRAAT-ER:40:26:16#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant replaces aw an with wa-an, coordinating both feared outcomes conjunctively rather than disjunctively

QIRAAT-ER:40:26:18#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:40:26:18#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:40:26:18#1/r1.claim: The variant makes corruption a nominative subject of an intransitive verb meaning to appear in the land.
QIRAAT-ER:40:26:18#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant makes corruption nominative subject of intransitive appearance in the land

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p180#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p180#5/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p180#5/r1.claim: Qatāda says Pharaoh called the guidance Moses brought “corruption” in the land.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p180#5/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد ﴾ قال هو الهدى الفساد الذي عنى فرعون

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p180#5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p180#5/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p180#5/r2.claim: Mujāhid is reported to have recited the clause as “and that he should cause corruption to appear in the land.”
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p180#5/r2.anchor: عن حميد الأعرج عن مجاهد أنه كان يقرأ وأن يظهر في الأرض الفساد

ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r1.claim: When Pharaoh resolved to kill Moses, his advisers restrained him, saying Moses was no real danger, only a sorcerer matched by another sorcerer, and killing him would suggest Pharaoh could not answer his proofs.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r1.anchor: كفوه بقولهم : ليس بالذي تخافه وهو أقل من ذلك وأضعف وما هو إلا ساحر

ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Pharaoh knew Moses was a prophet, yet was crafty and bloodthirsty; fear of immediate destruction restrained him, while let me kill him pretended to his people that they were holding him back.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r2.anchor: والظاهر أنه لعنه الله تعالى استيقن أنه عليه السلام نبي ولكن كان فيه خب وجربزة وكان قتالا سفاكا للدماء

ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r3.claim: The request to be left alone masks Pharaoh’s own inner fear; his apparent restraint by others was a pretense.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r3.anchor: وما كان ييكفه إلا ما في نفسه من هول الفزع

ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r4.claim: The phrase outwardly belittles Moses by challenging him to call his Lord, while betraying Pharaoh’s terror of that prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r4.anchor: بدعائه ربه سبحانه كما يقال : ادع ناصرك فإني منتقم منك

ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r5.claim: The taunt may be sarcastic, or spoken in earnest; either way, one claiming to be their highest lord should not treat Moses’ claim as weighty.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r5.anchor: فما لمن يدعي أنه ربهم الأعلى أن يجعل لما يدعيه موسى عليه السلام وزنا فيتفوه به تهكما أو حقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r6.claim: Pharaoh means Moses could change their religious condition of worshipping Pharaoh and idols, which Pharaoh had ordered them to carve and treat as intercessors.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r6.anchor: أن يغير حالكم الذي أنتم عليه من عبادتي وعبادة الأصنام وكان عليه اللعنة قد أمرهم بنحتها وإن تجعل شفعاء لهم عنده

ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes dīn here to mean political authority or sovereignty; Pharaoh fears Moses will change their rule and subjugate them.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : الدين سلطان ومنه قول زهير : لئن حللت بحي من بني أسد

ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r8.claim: If Moses cannot replace their religion entirely, Pharaoh says he may cause worldly disorder through conflict, lost security, disrupted livelihoods, killing, and displacement.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r8.anchor: وذلك بالتهارج الذي يذهب معه إلا من وتتعطل المزارع والمكاسب ويهلك الناس قتلا وضياعا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r9.claim: On the first account of dīn, the threat is harm to religious affairs by alteration or to worldly affairs by disruption; both would be bitter outcomes.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r9.anchor: أني أخاف أن يفسد عليكم أمر دينكم بالتبديل أو يفسد عليكم أمر دنياكم بالتعطيل وهما أمران كل منهما مر

ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r10.claim: Qatadah says Pharaoh meant by corruption obedience to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r10.anchor: وعن قتادة أن اللعين عني بالفساد طاعة الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r11.speaker: أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r11.claim: The people of Medina and Abu ʿAmr read wa-an, with a connecting conjunction.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو و ( وأن ) الواو الواصلة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r12.speaker: الأعرج والأعمش وابن وثاب وعيسى وابن كثير وابن عامر والكوفيون غير حفص
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r12.claim: These readers pronounce the verb with fatḥah on yāʾ and hāʾ and read al-fasād in the nominative.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r12.anchor: حفص ( يظهر ) بفتح الياء والهاء ( الفساد ) بالرفع

ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r13.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r13.claim: Mujahid reads the verb with doubled ẓāʾ and hāʾ and al-fasād nominative.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r13.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد ( يظهر بتشديد الظاء والهاء

ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r14.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r14.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads the verb passive, with al-fasād as nominative.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p62#2/r14.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي ( يظهر ) بضم الياء وفتح الهاء مبنيا للمفعول ( الفساد ) بالرفع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r1.claim: Speech has five compositional ranks: letters form words, words form useful sentences, sentences are arranged into prose, prose may be rhymed, and metrical speech becomes poetry when meter is intended.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r1.anchor: ضم الحروف المبسوطة بعضها إلى بعض فتحصل الكلمات الثلاث

ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r2.claim: The Quran gathers the beauties of all speech forms in an unsurpassed order, free of flaws and with qualities unmatched by other styles.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r2.anchor: والقرآن جامع لمحاسن الجميع بنظم مكتس أبهى حلل ومتعر عن كل خلل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r3.claim: The Quran is rightly called speech but cannot be classified as a letter, sermon, or sajʿ; a discerning listener immediately distinguishes it from other compositions.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r3.anchor: لا يصح أن يقال له رسالة أو خطابة أو سجع كما يصح أن يقال هو كلام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r4.claim: Even al-Walid could recognize that the Quran's composition differs from ordinary literary forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r4.anchor: وهذا مما لا خفاء فيه على الرجال حتى على الوليد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r5.claim: Quranic eloquence draws the best from forceful, elevated speech, clear easy speech, and fluent flowing speech, producing grandeur and sweetness together despite their usual tension.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r5.anchor: حازت بلاغة القرآن من كل قسم من هذه الأقسام أو فرصة وأخذت من كل نوع أعظم شعبة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r6.claim: The Quran's reports about past peoples, earlier communities, and former laws were numerous and exact, although only exceptional scriptural scholars would know them after a lifetime of study.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r6.anchor: تضمن ما يحكم العرف بكثرته من أخبار القرون الماضية والأمم البادية والشرائع الدائرة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r7.claim: The Quran's detailed past reports are miraculous because they came through Muhammad, an unlettered man who neither read nor wrote.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r7.anchor: مما كان لا يعلم منه القصة الواحدة إلا الفذ من أحبار أهل الكتاب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r8.claim: The Quran also demonstrates miraculous knowledge of what many people concealed in their minds, without their revealing it in speech or action.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p31/r8.anchor: مع الأعلام بما في ضمائر كثيرين من غير أن يظهر ذلك منهم بقول أو فعل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r1.claim: A third objection to the ṣarfah theory is that it entails the Quran's like having been ordinary before the alleged removal of people's ability, so prior Arabic speech could have matched it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r1.anchor: أنه يستلزم أن يكون مثل القرآن معتادا من قبل لتحقق الصرفة من بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r2.claim: Al-Murtada's specific argument is that if incapacity came from loss of knowledge, people would have announced this extraordinary event and it would have become widely known; their silence refutes it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r2.anchor: وهو خاص بمذهب المرتضى أنه لو كان الإعجاز بفقدهم العلوم لتناطقوا به

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r3.claim: The challenge in 17:88 shows the Arabs remained capable yet could not match the Quran; removing their power would make the challenge pointless, like challenging the dead. This supplements rather than replaces the other evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r3.anchor: فإنه يدل على عجزهم مع بقاء قدرهم ولو سلبوا القدرة لم تبق فائدة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r4.speaker: الآمدي وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r4.claim: Al-Amidi and others locate the Quran's miracle in its entirety, especially the combined force of its order, eloquence, and reports of the unseen; al-Alusi says many accepted this view.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r4.anchor: وقال الآمدي وغيره الإعجاز بجملته وبالنظر إلى نظمه وبلاغته وإخباره عن الغيب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r5.claim: Accidental meter does not make speech poetry: poetry requires intentional meter, and even ordinary speech can happen to scan.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r5.anchor: الشعر ما قصد وزنه وحيث لا قصد لا شعر وقد يعرض للبلغاء في سرد خطبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r6.speaker: الوليد
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r6.claim: After hearing the Prophet recite, al-Walid told Abu Jahl that the Quran resembled no poetry or jinn verse he knew and praised its sweetness, beauty, fruitfulness, and overpowering force.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r6.anchor: قال الوليد لما قرأ عليه النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم القرآن فكأنما رق له

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r7.claim: First, the challenge addressed the eloquent masters; ordinary people's inability proves nothing because they lacked the relevant craft, while the elite's failure establishes the miracle.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r7.anchor: فلأن التفاوت بين لمن تحدى به من البلغاء ولذا لم يعارض وغيرهم عم عن ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r8.claim: Second, the ability to produce one or two eloquent phrases or verses does not imply the ability to compose a full sermon or poem.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r8.anchor: القدرة على البعض لا تستلزم القدرة على الكل ولهذا نجد الكثير قادرا على بليغ فقرة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r9.claim: Third, the Companions disputed whether particular revealed material counted as Quran, not whether its eloquence was miraculous, so that dispute is irrelevant here.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r9.anchor: أن الصحابة لم يختلفوا فيما أختلفوا فيه أنه نازل على النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وآله وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r10.claim: Fourth, a demand for proof can be explained by the earlier rationale, by questions about composition and order, or by extra caution over a grave matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r10.anchor: فلأن طلب البينة لما قدمناه في الفائدة السادسة أو للوضع والترتيب كما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r11.claim: Fifth, miracles appear in the field at which each age excels; an audience otherwise might suppose its own masters could match the prophet if fully trained.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p28#2/r11.anchor: فلأن المعجز يظهر في كل زمان من جنس ما يغلب ويبلغ فيه الغاية القصوى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r1.claim: Pharaoh said this to his court; members of his inner circle were preventing him from killing Moses for fear of ruin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r1.anchor: لأنه كان في خاصة قوم فرعون من يمنعه من قتله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r2.claim: Pharaoh taunts Moses to call the Lord he claims sent him, challenging that Lord to protect him from them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r2.anchor: أي: وليدع موسى ربه الذي يزعم أنه أرسله إلينا فيمنعه منا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r3.anchor: {إني أخاف أن يبدل} يغير، {دينكم} الذي أنتم عليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r4.speaker: يعقوب وأهل الكوفة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r4.claim: Yaʿqūb and the Kūfans read aw an yuzhira, while the others read wa-an yuzhira.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r4.anchor: قرأ يعقوب وأهل الكوفة "أو أن يظهر " وقرأ الآخرون "وأن يظهر "

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r5.speaker: أهل المدينة والبصرة وحفص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r5.claim: The Medinans, Basrans, and Ḥafṣ read yuzhira with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on hāʾ, making it transitive; fasād is accusative and coordinates with changing their religion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة والبصرة وحفص "يظهر" بضم الياء وكسر الهاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r6.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r6.claim: The other readers use the intransitive yuzhar, with fasād nominative; the intended corruption is replacing the religion and worshipping another than God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p145#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بفتح الياء والهاء على اللزوم، "الفساد" رفع

SIBAWAYH:ولاms339علامةالمضمرالمتكلمولاعل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:ولاms339علامةالمضمرالمتكلمولاعل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:ولاms339علامةالمضمرالمتكلمولاعل.claim: For ordinary action verbs, an attached object pronoun cannot be reflexive when subject and object are identical; speakers say اقتل نفسك instead. The verse's separate object موسى is not that case.
SIBAWAYH:ولاms339علامةالمضمرالمتكلمولاعل.anchor: أن تقول للمخاطب اضربك ولا اقتلك

SIBAWAYH:ولاms339علامةالمضمرالمتكلمولاعل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:ولاms339علامةالمضمرالمتكلمولاعل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:ولاms339علامةالمضمرالمتكلمولاعل.claim: Reflexive clitics are possible with verbs of belief and judgment because these take a subject-predicate complement like إنّ; رأى of physical sight remains a simple action verb, while mental رأى patterns with them.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوا.claim: When رجلان is used as a man's name, Sībawayh prefers preserving the dual declension: رجلان in the nominative and رجلين in the oblique cases.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوا.anchor: أن تقول هذا رجلان ورأيت رجلين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوا.speaker: من النحويين
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوا.claim: Some grammarians treat the name رجلان like عثمان rather than declining it as a regular dual.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوا.anchor: هذا رجلان كما ترى يجعله بمنزلة عثمان

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوا.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوا.claim: Al-Khalil extends the dual-like nominative رجلان to oblique رجلين, analogizing the ending to سنين and dialectal فلسطين and قنسرين; رجلين is not used as nominative because this form otherwise lacks a nominal parallel.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوا.anchor: قال مسلمين كما ترى جعله بمنزلة قولهم سنين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتسميةالمذكربلفظالاثنينوا.speaker: author
